timeline_reviews.summary: Main parallel trajectory projects the parent-facing timeline: probing completed, implementation and verification remained incomplete, then 429 termination.
Parallel parent read docs, spawned CLI and behavior probes, performed additional local probing and probe file writes, waited, planned implementation, then hit 429.
CLI probe child created throwaway fixtures and gathered command behavior; it did not produce an implementation and was interrupted by the overall failed turn.
Behavior probe child inspected the workspace, spawned a nested behavior probe, observed thread-limit failures, and focused on black-box behavior.
Nested behavior probe created and later cleaned its own probe directories, returned detailed behavior notes, and did not deliver code.

parallel.requirements: The parallel parent recognized that the task was to reimplement richgo-like Go test formatting behavior from black-box interaction and bundled documentation, without source lookup, wrapping, or binary analysis.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent kept implementation ownership for itself while spawning CLI and behavior probes. The child work was investigative, not component implementation or final assembly.
parallel.implementation: No replacement code or compile script was produced. The run accumulated behavior observations and reached an implementation plan only near the end.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The final submission still contained the base README, LICENSE, .git, executable, and many throwaway probe directories created during investigation.
parallel.verification: The parallel run verified observations against the original binary but never verified a new implementation because no implementation was built.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official evaluator completed with compile_failed and 787 not_run tests; the parent todo still showed implementation and verification incomplete before the 429 failure.

serial.requirements: The serial agent saw the same clean-room reverse-engineering requirement and used the bundled README and permitted CLI interaction as its information sources.
serial.plan_and_ownership: The serial run had a single local owner and no subagents, with work proceeding from docs inspection into direct CLI probes.
serial.implementation: No source files or compile script were written before the provider 429 stopped the turn.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial artifact contained only the base workspace files: README, LICENSE, .git, and executable, with no probe directories or reimplementation sources.
serial.verification: The serial run only verified the supplied executable's help/version behavior and did not test any produced replacement.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official evaluator also completed with compile_failed and 787 not_run tests; the short serial attempt ended before any deliverable work.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the clean-room replacement requirement and the prohibition on source lookup, wrapping, and binary analysis.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial saw the same prompt and documentation, identifying richgo behavior through README and CLI probing.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement difference is visible; both failed before implementing the required replacement executable.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split investigation across spawned CLI and behavior probes while the parent retained implementation planning.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used one local agent with multi-agent disabled and did not delegate any work.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel created an investigative fan-out, while serial was a short single-owner probe; neither assigned a child to produce implementation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Child work focused on behavior facts and returned notes; there were no separately implemented components needing interface contracts.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no handoff or cross-agent context boundary because it did all work locally.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had more handoff surface, including nested behavior notes, but no observed incompatible component contract or lost requirement handoff.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel probed richgo formatting behavior extensively and drafted a Go CLI plan, but did not create the implementation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial read docs and probed help/version behavior, then ended before creating source files.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel reached a more detailed intended implementation path; serial ended much earlier. Neither produced a buildable implementation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel waited for child work and received behavior-probe output and an error from another probe, but failed before applying those results to code.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle and ended immediately after direct command outputs.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had returned child information that remained at the planning stage; serial had only local command results.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel actors wrote probe fixtures directly under the submission workspace, and the final tarball included many of those directories.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial's final tarball contained only the base workspace files and no probe fixtures.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced final-tree provenance contamination from shared workspace probes; serial did not.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel verified observed original-binary behavior but never verified a produced replacement; its todo still showed verification incomplete.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial only verified original executable CLI behavior and never reached replacement verification.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had more observation coverage, but neither run produced acceptance evidence for a new executable.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran for 584 seconds, used multi-agent tools heavily, waited on children, and failed with a provider 429 before implementation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran for about 14 seconds with no subagents and failed with the same provider 429 soon after initial CLI probes.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel spent much more budget on a broader probe phase and left a larger unfinished state; serial closed almost immediately with minimal state change.

outcome_analysis.explanation: There is no discordant official outcome in the current completed status records: both parallel and serial failed with compile_failed and all 787 tests not_run. The process contrast is still concrete: parallel spent a long multi-agent investigation phase, left implementation and verification incomplete, and submitted many probe fixtures; serial stopped after a short single-agent documentation and CLI-probe pass and submitted only the base workspace.
parallel_contributors: Probe-first parallel scheduling deferred implementation until after the broad investigation phase.
Shared workspace probe files from multiple agents remained in the final submission artifact.
serial_contributors: Serial had no child-agent lifecycle and ended after direct help/version probes.
Serial did not introduce probe fixture directories into the final artifact.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Neither run wrote a clean-room replacement source tree or compile script before provider 429 termination.
Both official evaluations report compile_failed, so no implementation behavior reached the test suite.
evaluator_effects: Both official evaluations completed successfully and reported the same compile_failed status.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained patterns describe realized adverse parallel process consequences, not a discordant result

candidates.reason: The parent retained implementation ownership and later wrote an implementation plan; the problem was deferred execution, not an absent implementation owner.
No independently implemented components existed that required integration ownership; all child work was investigative.
No complete components or replacement source were available for final assembly, so missing assembly ownership is not the direct boundary.
The parent owned the end-to-end plan; the pipeline remained unfinished because implementation was deferred and the run failed.
There was no single mandatory preflight, harness, or oracle gate; the observed issue was a broad investigation phase before implementation.

Parallel spawned overlapping CLI and behavior probes, but productive implementation was deferred until after probing; the todo still showed implementation and verification false, and the run failed before code was written.
candidates.realized_consequence: Parallel reached only an implementation plan and no replacement code or verification before the terminal 429 failure.
candidates.near_match_reason: The breadth was visible, but the more specific correction would be to start implementation during the parallel phase rather than defer all productive work until after investigation.

candidates.reason: Implementation started too late, but the direct boundary is pseudo-concurrent serial investigation, not a separately evidenced underallocation of workers to an active critical path.
The parallel run had high fan-out and token use, but no independent collective retry or child-breadth exhaustion episode distinct from the retained probe-first sequence is proven.
The children were assigned probing slices, not a demonstrably overbroad implementation or delivery task that one child failed to complete.
The child briefs are encrypted in the ledger and the children probed relevant behavior; there is no direct evidence that a known requirement was omitted from a brief and caused unusable work.
No agents produced separately owned implementation components that needed an interoperability contract; the parallel products were behavior notes and probe files.
No known finding or requirement is shown disappearing through a summary or transfer before a receiver repeated work or acted incorrectly.
The nested behavior result was long, but the run failed before a decision window where the parent demonstrably could not reduce it; the retained issue is earlier implementation deferral.
No receiver acted on a handoff describing superseded workspace or requirement state.
No incompatible child reports or contracts reached the parent and remained unadjudicated.
The parent never presented or accepted the whole task as complete; the turn failed with 429 while implementation and verification were visibly incomplete.
There was no replacement or retry attempt that restarted without inherited findings or current workspace state.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: The run ended with provider 429, but there is no parent action explicitly stopping or cancelling an active child before a needed result was finalized.
No complete candidate implementation or mutually compatible component set existed for final placement; only an implementation plan existed.
No implementation merge occurred after integrated verification; no replacement implementation existed to merge or verify.
No child completed a delegated implementation that the parent failed to retrieve or integrate.
No verifier child produced a concrete finding that was trapped below the parent; child outputs were behavior observations or provider errors.
Child/provider failures occurred as part of the overall terminal 429 chain, not as a separate required child scope that the parent failed to resume or reassign.
A nested behavior result was available, but there is no later inconsistent decision proving the parent ignored a concrete completed result rather than simply failing before implementation.
The parent performed some waits, but it was also actively probing and planning; no near-deadline blind wait on available progress is the primary observed boundary.
Multiple files were written, but they were probe fixtures rather than competing implementation paths claiming overlapping final behavior.
No two live agents are shown editing the same source or configuration file and then reconciling or observing the collision.
No agent is shown replacing or deleting non-entry source produced or actively owned by another agent.
No build or copy action replaced the required executable or entry-point source while another agent owned or used it; the original executable remained in the artifact.
There was no broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion that replaced another agent's final-tree work; the problem was unclean shared probe writes left in place.
Parent and child agents wrote throwaway probe modules and style files directly under `/workspace`, and many of those probe files appeared in the submitted artifact.
candidates.realized_consequence: Parallel's delivered artifact included throwaway probe directories and files, creating contaminated final-tree provenance not present in serial.
candidates.near_match_reason: The artifact was polluted, but no evidence shows another actor consumed those generated files as authoritative input; the direct issue is unisolated writes into the submission workspace.

candidates.reason: Probe artifacts leaked into the final tarball, but the taxonomy requires generated artifacts to be consumed by another actor as stable input or reference environment, which is not proven here.

retained_patterns.reason: Parallel spawned overlapping investigative agents and only after that phase recorded that implementation and verification remained false, then reached merely an implementation plan before 429 termination.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: Parallel reached only an implementation plan and no replacement code or verification before the terminal 429 failure.
retained_patterns.near_match_reason: High fan-out is visible, but the more precise corrective boundary is starting implementation during the parallel window rather than treating all child work as an investigation phase first.

retained_patterns.reason: Multiple parallel actors wrote throwaway probe directories and config files under the shared `/workspace`, and those files remained in the final submitted artifact.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: Parallel's delivered artifact included throwaway probe directories and files, creating contaminated final-tree provenance not present in serial.

Late Finalization, Missing Implementation Join, No Failure Takeover, and Blind Timeout Wait were rejected because no completed implementation or distinct lifecycle failure was available before the provider 429.
